**Create command for A**

```bash
(cd '/work/import queue' && LANDED_SUBJECT=$(cat '/work/import queue/.git/gauntlet/tmp/pr-body.B72pL3.title') && gh pr create --title "$LANDED_SUBJECT" --body-file '/work/import queue/.git/gauntlet/tmp/pr-body.B72pL3')
```

The file writer wrote the body as Markdown to the scratch path the mint printed. It wrote the landed subject ``Report a missing `id` in $(import)`` verbatim to that path with `.title` appended. The create call reads both files, the body through `--body-file` and the subject through a quoted variable. As a result, the shell never evaluates the backticks or `$(import)` and never treats `EOF` as a heredoc delimiter.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moved `create` and `update` as intended and kept `offer`. For `create`, the new body now carries the spec's Integration section verbatim once after Test Plan, with the indented instruction and the literal EOF and End of receipt lines, and adds no claim that any entry was checked. The command passes the minted path as one quoted `--body-file` argument, sets the worktree with its own `cd`, and reads the title from a file into a quoted variable, so the backticks and `$(import)` stay out of shell source (Before inlined the title in single quotes and omitted Integration). For `update`, After replaces only the stale Integration block with the current one, drops the screenshot entry, adds no Rework block, and leaves the double-spaced intro line and the Notes section untouched. The menu is identical in both outputs and asks nothing about Integration. One thing to tighten: the title file is an unminted sibling path (`<minted path>.title`) that only the closing prose explains. If the wording said explicitly where the title data file comes from (its own mint, or a stated derivation from the body path) and that the create call reads it within the same call, a reader would not wonder whether the command relies on an unminted path or earlier shell state. Keep the wording that makes the offer independent of Integration entries and that limits reconciliation on an existing PR to that one block, since those are what hold `offer` and `update`.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After moved create and update as intended and kept offer. The new PR body now carries the spec's Integration block verbatim once after Test Plan, including the indented instruction and the literal EOF and End of receipt lines, with no claim that any condition was checked. The draft body swaps only the stale Integration block for the current one, dropping the screenshot entry and leaving the double-spaced opening line and Notes untouched. The menu is unchanged, in order, and makes no mention of Integration. The create command runs in the quoted worktree, passes the minted path as one --body-file argument, and reads the title from a file into a quoted variable inside the same call, so title and body stay outside shell source and nothing depends on earlier shell state. Before had inlined the title in single quotes, which put it in shell source. One fragile point: the `.title` sibling path is derived from the minted body path rather than printed by the mint, and the output only asserts that the writer stored the literal subject there. To keep create holding, the wording should state explicitly that the title is written as data (never interpolated into shell) to a path derived from the minted body-file path, read back within the create call, and passed as one quoted --title argument. Keep the rule that the offer is independent of Integration entries and that an existing PR's reconciliation touches only that block.
